intro: Traditional dream meanings rewritten in plain contemporary English from four public-domain dream books (Project Gutenberg), with a modern reading of the feelings involved and questions for reflection.
The "tone" runs from ●○○○○ (very negative omen) to ●●●●● (very positive omen). The omens come from the old books: read them as cultural history, not prediction.
At the end, an index sends synonyms to their entries (e.g. "loaf → see BREAD").

entries.title: Dreaming of Abandonment
entries.one: A dream of abandonment is mostly about the future: plans that are hard to build, or ties you fear losing.
entries.tone_label: mostly negative, with one happy exception
situations: an unexpected inheritance, the one happy sign
you struggle to make plans for the future
a setback when you try your luck
lost valuables stay lost and friends turn away
You abandon your children or your business
losses and quarrels through lack of calm
a business failure, unless you make it to shore
feelings: the dream often reflects a worry about being left out
it may express a wish to leave a burden or situation behind
questions: Is there a relationship or project I feel slipping away?
Am I the one who wants to walk away from something?
entries.refs: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a Dream (1901)

entries.title: Dreaming of an Abbess

it may express a need for gentle guidance

Whose kind advice would I welcome?

entries.title: Dreaming of an Abbey

you are saved from ruin because rivals mistake your trouble for success
feelings: the dream may reflect regret over a plan left half-done
it may express a wish to shelter from the world
questions: What plan have I let fall into ruin?
Do I need a quiet place to find myself again?

entries.title: Dreaming of an Abbot

it may express a fear of having given in too easily to praise
questions: Who is flattering me right now, and why?

entries.title: Dreaming of the Abdomen
entries.one: The abdomen in a dream is about expectations, effort and worries over loved ones' health.

hardships, but you will overcome them and enjoy what you have earned
an accident or tragedy in the family
feelings: the dream often reflects concern about your own or your family's health
it may express a fear of being hurt where you are weakest
questions: What am I struggling to digest right now?
Am I taking good enough care of my body?

entries.title: Dreaming of Being Abroad

entries.title: Dreaming of a Zoo
entries.one: A zoo points to ups and downs in fortune and to knowledge gained through travel.
situations: a varied fortune, sometimes overpowered by enemies, sometimes at the front of success
you'll learn much from travel and time spent abroad
feelings: the dream often reflects a wish to discover and learn
it may mirror a sense of being watched or kept in
questions: How am I handling the ups and downs right now?
What would I like to discover?
entries.refs: G. H. Miller, Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted, or What's in a Dream (1901)

entries.title: Dreaming of Zouaves
entries.one: Zouaves, like other soldiers, point to family quarrels and disappointments in love.
situations: your sweetheart may love someone else more, or try to take advantage of your trust
Seeing zouaves or other armed soldiers
quarrels and trouble in your family or among relatives
feelings: the dream often reflects a climate of conflict at home
it may mirror a fear of not being loved back
questions: Which family conflict is on my mind?
Do I fully trust my relationship?
entries.refs: F. Fontaine, The Golden Wheel Dream-Book and Fortune-Teller (1862)
